newsitem.title: UK: Major says British govt can carry on as minority.
newsitem.headline: Major says British govt can carry on as minority.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Friday that his government could carry on in office despite the loss of its overall parliamentary majority.

"I think we can carry on," he said in a BBC Television interview. "The Callaghan government carried on for a long time as a minority government," he added, referring to the last Labour government under James Callaghan which lost power to the Conservatives in 1979.
"Of course it becomes more difficult when you don't have a clear-cut majority," Major said.
"When you have a small majority or no majority, every single rebellion is a drama...But again I think we can carry on and I intend to."
The prime minister declined to be drawn on a date for the next general election, which has to be held by May 22, 1997.
"I believe we can carry on until the date I wish to choose the election," he said.
